left_out_stems: A 10-year-old girl with sinus arrhythmia breathes in deeply. What happens to her heart rate?
A 21-year-old man with preexcitation has a short PR interval. Why is it short?
A 23-year-old man's report reads benign early repolarization. Which other name does this pattern carry?
A 24-year-old woman's tracing shows a delta wave. What causes the slurring?
A 30-year-old woman's impulse reaches her Purkinje fibers. What is distinctive about how they conduct?
A 32-year-old man has antidromic reentrant tachycardia. Which rhythm can it be impossible to tell apart from on the tracing alone?
A 33-year-old man is diagnosed with pericarditis. Which space is inflamed?
A 33-year-old woman's ventricular cell is at rest in phase 4. What is the voltage inside the cell?
A 36-year-old woman has hyperthyroidism. Which tracing finding is the most commonly observed?
A 39-year-old man has first-degree atrioventricular block. How many of his P waves are conducted to the ventricles?
A 45-year-old man's PR interval is measured. What span does the PR interval cover?
A 48-year-old woman has the 12-lead shown: a long, flat ST segment before a normally shaped T wave. Which electrolyte disturbance does it suggest?
A 53-year-old woman's atrioventricular node delays each impulse. Which zone slows conduction and can serve as the backup pacemaker?
A 54-year-old man has ST elevation in V1, V2 and V3. Which walls do these contiguous leads look at?
A 55-year-old man has an episode of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that twists around the baseline. Which interval abnormality is it usually a consequence of?
A 57-year-old man has ST-segment elevation in II, III and aVF. Which process does the elevation represent?
A 57-year-old woman's myocytes are contracting. During which action potential phase does calcium enter the cell?
A 57-year-old woman's serum calcium is low, 7.4 mg/dL (reference range 8.5 to 10.5). Why does her ST segment lengthen?
A 58-year-old man is learning his conduction system. Into which three fascicles does the left bundle branch split?
A 59-year-old man has a regular narrow tachycardia at 150 per minute (normal 60 to 100). Which finding would make it atrial flutter rather than the reentry tachycardia?
A 59-year-old man has an isolated posterior wall infarction. About what share of acute myocardial infarctions are isolated posterior infarctions?
A 61-year-old man has ST elevation in I, aVL and V3 to V6. Which region does this localize to?
A 61-year-old man has many cells capable of automaticity. What normally keeps the lower ones from firing?
A 61-year-old man's strip is shown. What pattern do his premature beats follow?
A 62-year-old man develops a new intraventricular conduction abnormality. Which one is most common during an acute myocardial infarction?
A 62-year-old woman's 12-lead is being read wall by wall. Which lead is not assigned to any wall?
A 62-year-old woman's monitor prints this strip. What is the rhythm?
A 64-year-old man has an infarction with no facing lead on the standard 12-lead. Which leads carry its reciprocal changes?
A 64-year-old woman has chest pain and the 12-lead shown. Which region does the ST elevation localize to?
A 64-year-old woman's cardiologist calls her rhythm Mobitz I. Which block is that?
A 66-year-old man's ST segment is being compared with baseline. Which segment best shows the true isoelectric line?
A 67-year-old man has Wenckebach block in his atrioventricular node. What happens to conduction through the node from beat to beat?
A 68-year-old man is placed on a cardiac monitor. Why is lead II used for rhythm interpretation?
A 68-year-old man with chest pain develops complete heart block. Which infarct location is especially associated with it?
A 68-year-old man's monitor shows polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Which rate and regularity fit it?
A 68-year-old woman has this electrocardiogram. Which conduction abnormality does it show?
A 68-year-old woman is told the artery that supplies the back of her septum is blocked. Which artery is it?
A 69-year-old woman's chest leads are measured for left ventricular hypertrophy. Which single-lead finding meets a criterion?
A 70-year-old man has a bundle branch block. Why is his QRS wide?
A 70-year-old man has a wandering atrial pacemaker. How many P wave shapes define it?
A 70-year-old woman with a recent infarction has this complex in V2: a single deep negative deflection with no R wave. In this setting, what is it called?
A 71-year-old man in cardiac arrest has pulseless electrical activity. Which statement about its appearance is correct?
A 71-year-old man is paced only by his Purkinje network. What intrinsic rate should be expected?
A 71-year-old man with a ventricular paced rhythm has chest pain. Which finding meets Sgarbossa's criteria?
A 72-year-old man has an inferior infarction. Which findings should raise suspicion of right ventricular involvement?
A 72-year-old man has an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia. Which finding favors multifocal atrial tachycardia over atrial fibrillation?
A 72-year-old man with long-standing lung disease has right axis deviation. Which is a listed cause?
A 72-year-old woman has left ventricular hypertrophy. Which axis change does it cause?
A 72-year-old woman's QRS is 0.12 seconds or longer (normal under 0.12). Her V1 and V6 complexes are shown. Which block is this?
A 73-year-old man has a regular escape rhythm with no P waves. Which feature best separates junctional from idioventricular origin?
A 74-year-old man has second-degree type II block. Where is the block usually located?
A 75-year-old man has a wide QRS with notched lateral complexes and no Q waves in I, aVL, V5 and V6. Which block is this?
A 75-year-old man has third-degree atrioventricular block. How do his atrial and ventricular rates compare?
A 76-year-old woman has atrial flutter. Which atrial change sets up its circuit?
A 76-year-old woman has this electrocardiogram. Which conduction abnormality does it show?
A 78-year-old woman's core temperature is falling toward 35°C (95°F; normal is about 37°C). Which tracing change occurs first?
A 79-year-old woman has ventricular escape complexes. Which failure produces them?
A 79-year-old woman is suspected of idioventricular rhythm. Which combination defines it?
A healthy 8-year-old girl has sinus arrhythmia on a sports physical. What does the finding usually mean?
Two patients each have a regular rhythm at 80 per minute (normal 60 to 100) with no P waves; one has wide complexes. What is the wide one?
